root_cause.text: In ath12k link-removal error handling, `ath12k_mac_op_change_vif_links()` skipped cleanup for initialized-but-not-created `arvif` objects by gating deletion on `arvif->is_created`, leaving a stale `ahvif->links_map`/link-vif mapping for the old link ID.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that when MLO prep fails before `arvif` creation, “link deletion only executes when `arvif->is_created` is true” and “ahvif retains a stale entry of arvif,” and the patch fixes this by adding `ath12k_mac_unassign_link_vif(arvif);` inside the `if (!arvif->is_created)` path before `continue`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit states that when MLO prep fails before `arvif` creation, “link deletion only executes when `arvif->is_created` is true” and “ahvif retains a stale entry of arvif,” and the patch fixes this by adding `ath12k_mac_unassign_link_vif(arvif);` inside the `if (!arvif->is_created)` path before `continue`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Unassign uncreated link VIFs before skipping them to avoid stale link association state.
intent_record.what: The change adds braces around the `if (!arvif->is_created)` branch and inserts a call to `ath12k_mac_unassign_link_vif(arvif);` before the existing `continue;` statement.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when a virtual interface link object exists but has not been created, the code now explicitly unassigns the link vif before skipping further processing. This prevents stale or leftover link-vif association state from remaining in place for uncreated links.

grouping_result.intent: Unassign uncreated link VIFs before skipping them to avoid stale link association state.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by unassigning initialized-but-not-created link VIFs before skipping deletion, which cleans up stale link association state that was previously left behind when deletion was gated on `arvif->is_created`.

candidates.rationale: This condition is the direct root cause: it gates cleanup/removal logic on creation state, so initialized-but-not-created arvif objects are skipped and their old link association state remains stale.
This statement performs the problematic skip when arvif->is_created is false, bypassing unassignment/cleanup and leaving ahvif->links_map and link-vif mapping for the old link ID intact.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition gates the link-removal cleanup path on creation state. For initialized-but-not-created arvif objects, it causes the function to skip cleanup, leaving stale ahvif->links_map and link-vif association state for the old link ID.
This skip statement is the operational trigger of the bug: when the preceding is_created check is false, execution bypasses unassignment and cleanup of the old link mapping, preserving stale state.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient because it contains the exact link-removal logic in `ath12k_mac_op_change_vif_links()` relevant to the root cause. In the newly added removal loop, the code computes `to_remove = old_links & ~new_links;` and then iterates: `for_each_set_bit(link_id, &to_remove, IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS)`. Inside that loop it fetches the link vif with `arvif = wiphy_dereference(hw->wiphy, ahvif->link[link_id]);` and then explicitly skips cleanup when `!arvif->is_created` via `if (!arvif->is_created) continue;`. Only when `is_created` is true does it run `ath12k_mac_remove_link_interface(hw, arvif);` and `ath12k_mac_unassign_link_vif(arvif);`. This matches the described vulnerable construct: initialized-but-not-created `arvif` objects are not cleaned up during link removal, so stale `ahvif->links_map` / link-vif mapping can remain for the old link ID. Therefore the bug is present. The fix is not present because correct handling would need to unassign/clean the link-vif mapping even when `arvif->is_created` is false, but this version gates all cleanup on `is_created` and simply `continue`s otherwise.
